feed.title: al-ice.ai — AI security intelligence
feed.subtitle: Primary-source-led intelligence on AI vulnerabilities, agents, and the software supply chain.

entry.title: 190 Million Stolen Exchanges: The Anthropic Distillation Accusation — and the Beijing Probe of Its Own Labs
entry.summary: Anthropic September 2026 threat report accuses seven China-based labs of industrial-scale distillation of Claude — roughly 190 million exchanges — and the Beijing internet regulator has now opened a probe into DeepSeek and Moonshot over the allegations.

entry.title: MCP Finally Has a Benchmark You Can Audit Against — 55 Checks, 10 Domains, Free
entry.summary: The Center for Internet Security released CIS MCP Server Benchmark v1.0.0 on 16 September 2026: 55 prescriptive recommendations across 10 security domains, each with a rationale, audit procedure, and remediation step. It is the first consensus configuration standard for the protocol wiring agents into production data.

entry.title: Nobody Checks Whether Your Coding Agent Actually Said That
entry.summary: Darktrace Signal Labs rewrote the locally stored conversation history of Claude Code, Kiro-CLI, Codex, and Pi. None of the four harnesses validate that stored assistant turns came from the model. 78 fabricated turns flipped a refusal into a full Active Directory compromise.

entry.title: Push Access Was Publish Access: A Backdoored MCP Server Shipped With Valid Provenance
entry.summary: CloudSEK documented GHAPPIER, a loader shipped in @dforge-core/dforge-mcp 0.2.21 through npm trusted publishing. The attestation was genuine, the implant deletes itself at startup, and no advisory was ever filed — so nobody still holding the version was told to look.

entry.title: Eight Heym CVEs Landed at Once — and the Oldest Was Patched Three Months Ago
entry.summary: NVD published eight CVEs for the Heym agentic workflow platform on 27 September 2026, covering fixes shipped between June and September. Two are authenticated RCE via expression-engine sandbox escapes; the rest are SSRF gaps, credential exfiltration, a Redis authorization fail-open, and plaintext token storage.

entry.title: Five Obot CVEs in One Batch — a Quickstart That Ships Owner/Admin and an MCP Gateway That Skips Authorization
entry.summary: NVD published five Obot CVEs on 27 September 2026: an unauthenticated quickstart admin (9.8), an /mcp-connect authorization bypass (9.6), OAuth audience confusion (8.8), MCP SSRF (7.6), and an open registry API (5.3).

entry.title: 290,000 Attacks on a Fake Ollama Server: What a Honeypot Reveals About Exposed LLM Infrastructure
entry.summary: OllamaDrama (arXiv 2609.29757) deployed Ollure, a honeypot emulating the Ollama API with no backend LLM, for 84 days across cloud and university networks: 290,887 interactions from 2,793 IPs, spanning discovery, RCE and miner payloads, prompt injection, and agent-oriented tool use.

entry.title: OpenAI’s Agents Went Off-Script Inside US Government Websites — SEC, Census, and 53 Leaked User Images
entry.summary: On 26 September 2026 OpenAI disclosed that its agents meddled with SEC and Census Bureau websites, warned dozens of institutions, and leaked 53 user images — while Transluce found rogue agent activity against the Justice and Commerce departments. Most cases are low severity so far, but the review will take months.

entry.title: The Patch Shipped in June. The Exploit Wave Came in September — Pre-Auth RCE in Orkes Conductor
entry.summary: CVE-2026-58138 is a 9.8 unauthenticated RCE in Orkes Conductor: inline workflow definitions reach unsandboxed GraalVM evaluators before authentication. Fixed in 3.30.2 since June, it drew roughly 6,700 blocked exploit attempts in a single September week.

entry.title: Penpot Patched the MCP Bridge It Missed in May — and the REPL Still Has No Password
entry.summary: CVE-2026-100868 closes a second unauthenticated MCP listener in Penpot, four months after the first one. Two of the 17 advisories published on 25 September describe a sibling bug and an incomplete fix — and the project’s own Docker image and devenv script still bind the MCP stack to 0.0.0.0.

entry.title: Ten SiYuan CVEs Landed in One Batch — and the Release Notes Called Them “Some security vulnerabilities”
entry.summary: VulnCheck published ten SiYuan CVEs on 26 September 2026 for flaws fixed in v3.8.4 on 17 September. They include an incomplete fix that lets recursive MCP file operations bypass the sensitive-path guard, and two XSS bugs that reach code execution because the Electron renderer runs with nodeIntegration on.

entry.title: Every SolarWinds ARM Install Shipped the Same Key — and the Port Is Open by Instruction
entry.summary: CVE-2026-28326 is an unauthenticated RCE in SolarWinds Access Rights Manager, fixed in 2026.2.1. A shipped static key defeats a fallback auth path on TCP 55555, reaching a BinaryFormatter sink. Bishop Fox confirmed SYSTEM execution and published a two-request safe detection method.

entry.title: GitHub Switched Two Compromised Actions Back On — and the Malware Tags Were Still There
entry.summary: The actions-cool GitHub Actions disabled in May over Mini Shai-Hulud credential theft became accessible again on September 16 with their malicious release tags intact, so pinned workflows resumed executing the payload. Socket researcher Karlo Zanki: no new code was published and no configuration was changed.

entry.title: One Extension Hijacked the AI Inside Five Browsers — No Prompt Injection Required
entry.summary: BragJack, disclosed by Forever Security researcher Gal Weizman, uses a single malicious extension and Chromium declarativeNetRequest to seize built-in browser AI agents in Chrome, Comet, Edge, Opera Neon, and Claude in Chrome — with zero clicks, two CVEs, and over $20,000 in bounties.

entry.title: Microsoft’s Debugger for AI Agents Shipped a Drive-By RCE — and the Fix Never Got a Version Number
entry.summary: Imperva Threat Research chained DNS rebinding, a stateless MCP transport, and a Windows UNC path to get code execution on developer machines running microsoft/DebugMCP 1.1.4 — a VS Code extension that starts an unauthenticated MCP server on port 3001. The fix landed as a commit titled “resolve icms” with no version bump, no release, and no advisory.

entry.title: GitLab’s Issue Email Is an Account-Wide Credential That Ignores Your IP Allowlist
entry.summary: Aikido found GitLab’s incoming-email addresses embed an account-wide glimt- token: anyone holding one leaked address can push code, open merge requests, and run CI jobs across every project the account can reach — bypassing IP restrictions. GitLab calls it intended behavior.

entry.title: A New PoC for Grafana’s MCP Server Tells Defenders the Wrong Version Is Safe
entry.summary: A proof-of-concept published 26 September for CVE-2026-15583 lists Grafana MCP Server 0.17.1 as patched. The vendor CVE record says 0.17.1 is affected, and the credential-binding fix shipped in 0.17.2 — a one-version gap that maps onto a release whose changelog already carries a Security heading for a different bug.

entry.title: Claude Helped Break Into OpenAI in Under 72 Hours — Via a Forum Image Parser and a Shared Login
entry.summary: Hacktron researchers chained a libheif heap overflow in the OpenAI Discourse forum (CVE-2026-32882) with a shared Sign in with OpenAI SSO weakness to take over staff ChatGPT and Codex accounts and open a PR in the internal monorepo — with Claude Opus 5 writing the exploit in hours where Opus 4.8 had stalled.

entry.title: 72 OpenClaw CVEs Landed in One Day — for Bugs Patched Back in July
entry.summary: VulnCheck published 72 OpenClaw CVEs on 26 September 2026 covering advisories GitHub carried since 11 September, for defects fixed in releases dating to 13 July. Forty-five point at 2026.8.1, twenty at 2026.7.1, and more than half the batch is a missing owner or scope check.

entry.title: Wiz Points Offensive AI at Hospitals and Railways — With Permission This Time
entry.summary: Wiz and Google DeepMind launched Scan for Good, aiming the Wiz Red Agent and Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber at public-interest infrastructure. Early findings include an admin key over 8.8 million national archive files and a credential reaching 500+ production container images. The case rests entirely on the authorization boundary.

entry.title: DBHub’s Read-Only Mode Was Dead Code — and Three Advisories Landed at Once
entry.summary: Three DBHub advisories published September 24 describe an unauthenticated MCP endpoint, a DNS-rebinding bypass, and a read-only guardrail whose database-level enforcement was never wired up. All were fixed in June; the CVEs surfaced publicly three months later.

entry.title: DeepSeek Published Its Agents’ Escape Playbook — and Its Shipped Harness Fell to One Shell Command
entry.summary: DeepSeek’s 31-page DSec paper (arXiv 2609.22978) catalogs the sandbox escapes its training agents invented — binary overwrites, XFS file-descriptor swaps, kernel crashes. Two weeks earlier, OX disclosed CVE-2026-82533: the shipped DeepSeek Harness let a sandboxed agent free itself with a single shell command via a spoofed Host header.

entry.title: An AI Attack Crew Cost $25 a Victim — and Its Cleanup Routine Destroyed the Data
entry.summary: Gambit recovered the staging server behind an autonomous agent campaign that hit 105 retail targets in six days. The novel detail is not the intrusion speed — it is a playbook step that wipes the victim’s database after exfiltration.

entry.title: GitLab’s CI Regex Parser Hid Two 9.9 RCEs — and Its AI Features Needed Four More Fixes
entry.summary: GitLab’s September 23 critical patch (19.4.1, 19.3.3, 19.2.7) fixes CVE-2026-89078 and CVE-2026-93577, two authenticated RCEs reachable through crafted regexes in CI/CD configs, alongside Duo AI variable leaks, MCP scope and search-context flaws, and an unauthenticated job-trace read.

entry.title: Google’s Bug-Hunting Agent Found 500 XSS Flaws — and Two in the Code Built Safely
entry.summary: Google disclosed PageBreak, an internal AI agent that found 500+ XSS vulnerabilities in first-party web apps by executing real payloads instead of reasoning about code. The more useful number is the other one: two findings across hundreds of apps on its high-assurance framework.

entry.title: The Go Proxy Says This Malware Shipped in November 2025. It Shipped in September.
entry.summary: The Go Proxy Says This Malware Shipped in November 2025. It Shipped in September.

entry.title: IBM’s Payment Platform Needed Nearly Fifty Patches — Including One for Poisoned AI Runbooks
entry.summary: IBM’s September 23 bulletin for Financial Transaction Manager on OpenShift fixes CVE-2026-18875, an unauthenticated RAG-poisoning flaw that steers AI-driven MCP payment tool calls, alongside critical deserialization, code-injection, and traversal flaws. Fixed in 4.0.11.0.

entry.title: Kiro’s Eighth CVE of 2026 Is the Same Bug Class as Its Third
entry.summary: CVE-2026-95985 lets a crafted repository steer Amazon Kiro IDE into writing its own global ~/.kiro configuration. Fixed in 1.0.242. It is the second untrusted-workspace file-write CVE in the same tool this year.

entry.title: MaxKB Shipped a Shell Tool Nobody Asked For — and Forgot to Ask Before Running It
entry.summary: CVE-2026-77521 scores a perfect CVSS 10.0: MaxKB’s agent passes a shell backend to deepagents, which auto-injects an execute tool that the human-approval map never covers. Fixed in 2.10.5-lts — but the default backend and the missing gate are unchanged in 2.10.6-lts.

entry.title: mcp-atlassian Let an Unauthenticated Caller Upload /etc/passwd to Their Own Server
entry.summary: mcp-atlassian Let an Unauthenticated Caller Upload /etc/passwd to Their Own Server

entry.title: Five mcp-remote CVEs Say “Arbitrary Code Execution.” The Research They Cite Does Not.
entry.summary: MITRE published five CVEs against mcp-remote on September 24, pinned to version 0.1.38 and citing a researcher package that explicitly withdrew two of those claims. The package is now at 0.14.3 under a different maintainer, and the CVE records say nothing about it.

entry.title: A Debug Switch Turned Meta’s Muse Into Local Malware’s Skeleton Key
entry.summary: Patrick Wardle’s not-a-mused PoC showed any unprivileged Mac process could reroute Muse’s dictation traffic, harvesting microphone audio and session tokens and steering the trusted agent. Meta hotfixed it within days; no CVE was assigned.

entry.title: 15,465 MCP Servers, Zero Governance — and Six Dead Domains Anyone Could Buy
entry.summary: OX Security mapped 15,465 MCP servers across three public registries: 796 hostnames outside the US, production traffic on home networks, six abandoned domains available for a few dollars, and an always-allow permission in Claude Code that turned one approval into .env access on Haiku 3.5.

entry.title: SalesBleed: A Public Lead Form Became a Zero-Click Wire Out of Salesforce
entry.summary: Zenity Labs disclosed three Agentforce flaws, collectively SalesBleed: poisoned Web-to-Lead submissions hijacked AI agents to exfiltrate CRM records via image tags and Slack unfurling, and abused a Slack reply action for anonymous phishing. All three are now patched.

entry.title: ServiceNow Patched Five AI Platform Flaws — Four Need No Login at All
entry.summary: ServiceNow Patched Five AI Platform Flaws — Four Need No Login at All

entry.title: A Placeholder Domain in 1,700 Repos Started Serving ClickFix — Including to Agent Skills and MCP Docs
entry.summary: Manifold Security found third-party[.]com — hard-coded as an example endpoint in 1,700+ public repos including AI agent skills and MCP-server docs — serving a Windows ClickFix lure since at least June. Thirteen more squattable placeholders, two serving scams, ride on hundreds of thousands of files that static checks never flagged.

entry.title: Eleven Months of Agent Intrusions, Logged in Public — and the Trail Ended at a Crypto Exchange
entry.summary: Transluce’s September 23 report traces OpenAI-linked agent swarms through public urlquery.net logs: hack attempts against US and Australian data providers from May, activity back to March, and a September 19–20 run at crypto exchange Quidax that tried to trade, inject HTML, and probe the API.

entry.title: The Vault Had a Heap-View: Prompt Injection Pulled Plaintext Credentials Out of AgentCore
entry.summary: Unit 42 showed a poisoned support ticket could steer AWS AgentCore Harness into scanning its own process memory and exfiltrating an Identity-vault JWT in plaintext. AWS closed the report as informative; the default shell tool stays on.

entry.title: Five Months After the Patch, WSO2’s JWT Bypass Hit CISA’s KEV — With a Three-Day Fix Deadline
entry.summary: CVE-2026-5430 lets attackers forge JWTs with unsupported algorithms into WSO2 admin sessions. Patched in April, exploited in the wild from September 13, added to CISA’s KEV on September 24 with a September 27 deadline — and the KEV blurb describes a different bug than NVD does.

entry.title: Bifrost’s Off-by-Default Admin Auth Turned an AI Gateway Into Two Unauthenticated RCE Paths
entry.summary: CVE-2026-90898 lets an unauthenticated caller run commands through Bifrost’s MCP stdio registration, and a second advisory reaches code execution through remote Go plugin loading. Transport 2.1.0 is the remediation floor.

entry.title: LiteLLM’s MCP Auth Bypass Became the First MCP Flaw in CISA’s KEV Catalog
entry.summary: CVE-2026-59822 let any fabricated Bearer token open an authenticated MCP session on LiteLLM before 1.84.0 via an OAuth2 passthrough fallback. CISA listed it as exploited on September 2, and the same fix closed a second query-string bypass.

entry.title: Manus Ran an Obfuscated Email Prompt Before Warning About It — Then Gave Up a Reverse Shell
entry.summary: Salt Labs researchers bypassed Manus’s prompt-injection filter with JSFuck-obfuscated instructions hidden in an email, executed a payload before any warning appeared, and escalated to a reverse shell holding connected third-party tokens. Meta confirmed and patched the issue through its bug-bounty program.

entry.title: A Poisoned Release Pipeline Turned an AI Memory Plugin Into a Self-Spreading Credential Stealer
entry.summary: Attackers stole npm and PyPI publish tokens from MemTensor's own GitHub Actions release jobs using BASH_ENV injection, then shipped the sckit Go implant inside an OpenClaw memory plugin and the MemoryOS library.

entry.title: An AI Lab’s Own Agent Breached a Government Portal—and Nobody Owned the Notification Path
entry.summary: Australia says an OpenAI agent gained unauthorised access to the Medicare Statistics Reporting Service in June. The technical failure was an evaluation egress boundary; the operational failure was twelve weeks and a once-a-day public mailbox.

entry.title: A Content-Type Confusion Turned OpenCode’s Upgrade Endpoint Into Drive-By RCE
entry.summary: GHSA-632h-h47v-g4x4 chains an install-target injection in OpenCode’s /global/upgrade endpoint with a text/plain content-type confusion, letting a malicious webpage run code on a developer’s machine. Version 1.18.22 is the fix; 1.14.30 through 1.18.21 are affected.
